title: Enable ESLint enforcement in CI pipeline
description:
## Context

ESLint configuration is complete but enforcement is currently disabled in CI to avoid blocking pre-demo work.

## What Needs to be Done

1. **Enable ESLint in CI Workflow** (5 min)
   * Uncomment lines 42-44 in `.github/workflows/type-safety.yml`
   * Test with a sample PR
2. **Fix ESLint Violations** (2-4 hours)
   * Current violations found in:
     * TEMP/app/availability-results/page.tsx
     * TEMP/app/book/checkout/page.tsx
     * TEMP/app/book/confirmation/page.tsx
   * Run `npm run lint -- --fix` for auto-fixes
   * Manually review and fix remaining violations
3. **Establish Baseline**
   * Document violation count
   * Set zero-violation policy for new code

## Resources

* Notion doc: Post-Demo CI/CD Tasks - PRIORITY
* ESLint config: `eslint.config.mjs`
* Run locally: `npm run lint`

## Timeline

* Day 1 (Post-Demo): Enable in CI, baseline report
* Days 2-3: Fix critical violations
* Days 4-5: Fix remaining violations

## Success Criteria

title: Production Deployment & Monitoring Setup
description:
## Description

Deploy refactored middleware to production with proper monitoring, rollback plan, and observability.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Rollback plan documented (how to revert to old middleware)
- [ ] Feature flag created for gradual rollout (if applicable)
- [ ] Monitoring alerts configured for middleware errors
- [ ] Logging enhanced for middleware execution (auth, tenant, wizard events)
- [ ] Error tracking configured (Sentry/equivalent for middleware errors)
- [ ] Production smoke tests pass after deployment
- [ ] Runbook created for on-call engineers

## Technical Context

* Environment: Production (Vercel/equivalent)
* Monitoring: Vercel Analytics, Sentry, custom logging
* Rollback: Git revert + immediate redeploy

## Deployment Checklist

1. **Pre-Deployment**
   - [ ] All tests passing (unit, integration, e2e, security)
   - [ ] `npm run verify:full` passes
   - [ ] Performance benchmarks reviewed
   - [ ] Rollback plan reviewed and approved
   - [ ] Team notified of deployment window
2. **Deployment**
   - [ ] Deploy to staging first
   - [ ] Run smoke tests on staging
   - [ ] Deploy to production
   - [ ] Monitor for 30 minutes post-deployment
3. **Post-Deployment**
   - [ ] Verify no error spikes in monitoring
   - [ ] Check auth flow working
   - [ ] Check wizard flow working
   - [ ] Check multi-tenant operations working
   - [ ] Verify no redirect loop incidents

## Monitoring

* Alert on: 401/403 error rate spikes
* Alert on: Redirect loop detection (>3 redirects)
* Alert on: Middleware execution time >200ms (p95)
* Log: Auth events, tenant context resolution, wizard access attempts

## Rollback Triggers

* Auth failure rate >5%
* Redirect loop incidents >2
* Critical error rate >1%
* Response time degradation >50%

## Verification

- [ ] Deployment successful
- [ ] Monitoring showing healthy metrics
- [ ] No incidents reported

title: Performance Testing & Optimization
description:

- [ ] Middleware execution time measured per layer (auth, tenant, wizard)
- [ ] Memory usage profiled and compared to baseline
- [ ] No performance regression detected (≤5% degradation acceptable)
- [ ] Optimization opportunities identified and documented
- [ ] Performance report created with metrics and recommendations

## Technical Context

* Tools: Artillery for load testing, Node.js profiler for memory
* Metrics: Response time (p50, p95, p99), throughput, error rate
* Scenarios: Login flow, wizard access, dashboard access, multi-tenant operations

## Performance Tests

1. **Baseline Measurement** (before refactor)
   * Auth middleware execution time
   * Full request cycle time
   * Memory consumption
2. **Refactored Measurement** (after refactor)
   * Same metrics as baseline
   * Compare and analyze differences
3. **Load Testing**
   * 100 concurrent users
   * Mix of auth, wizard, dashboard requests
   * Measure: throughput, latency, error rate

## Deliverables

* Performance test script (`tests/performance/middleware-perf.test.ts`)
* Load test configuration (Artillery config)
* Performance report (`docs/performance/middleware-refactor-results.md`)

## Verification

- [ ] No critical performance regressions
- [ ] Results documented and reviewed

title: Security Testing: Tenant Isolation & Auth Bypass
description:
## Description

Create security-focused tests ensuring no auth bypass vulnerabilities or tenant data leakage in refactored middleware.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Security tests created in `tests/security/middleware-security.test.ts`
- [ ] Test: Unauthenticated user cannot bypass auth to access protected routes
- [ ] Test: Tenant A cannot access Tenant B's data via middleware manipulation
- [ ] Test: Session token manipulation detected and rejected
- [ ] Test: Wizard access control cannot be bypassed
- [ ] Test: Direct URL access to protected routes properly redirects
- [ ] All existing tenant isolation tests still pass (16/16)
- [ ] `npm run test:security` passes with all tests green

## Technical Context

* Follow: [CLAUDE.md](http://CLAUDE.md) T-7, T-12 (multi-tenant security testing)
* Location: `tests/security/middleware-security.test.ts`
* Reference: Existing tests in `tests/security/tenant-isolation.test.ts`
* Tools: Attempt malicious requests, verify proper rejection

## Attack Scenarios to Test

* **Auth Bypass**: Remove auth token, attempt protected route access
* **Session Hijacking**: Use expired/invalid session token
* **Tenant Hopping**: Authenticated as Tenant A, try to access Tenant B's /dashboard
* **Wizard Bypass**: User with completed property tries to POST to wizard endpoints
* **Direct DB Access**: Verify RLS policies block cross-tenant queries
* **Parameter Tampering**: Modify tenant_id in request, verify rejection

## Verification

- [ ] All attack scenarios properly blocked
- [ ] Error messages don't leak sensitive information
- [ ] Audit logs created for security violations (if implemented)

title: Setup Wizard Stabilization
description:
## Overview

Epic to track all work required to stabilize the Setup Wizard and ensure reliable onboarding for new campground operators.

## Context

During the Oct 30, 2025 investor demo, critical failures occurred in the Setup Wizard that required manual browser refreshes at every step. This epic encompasses both the infrastructure hardening (middleware) and UI functionality fixes needed to prevent future incidents and deliver a production-ready onboarding experience.

## Business Impact

* **Investor Confidence**: Reliable demo experience for funding conversations
* **User Onboarding**: Smooth conversion from signup to active campground operator
* **Revenue**: Reduced drop-off during critical payment setup step
* **Support**: Fewer stuck users requiring manual intervention

## Scope

This epic includes:

1. **Middleware Hardening** (CAM-129)
   * Architectural improvements to prevent redirect loops
   * Explicit state machine for wizard access control
   * Type-safe route configuration
   * Comprehensive testing infrastructure
2. **Wizard Navigation & Skip Functionality** (CAM-130)
   * Fix navigation buttons (back/previous functionality)
   * Allow return to skipped steps (e.g., Stripe setup)
   * Improve UX for guest booking link placement
   * Ensure no user can become permanently stuck

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Complete wizard flow works end-to-end without manual intervention
- [ ] Users can navigate freely between all wizard steps
- [ ] Skipped steps can be completed later (in wizard or dashboard)
- [ ] Zero redirect loops or infinite loading states
- [ ] All critical paths covered by E2E tests
- [ ] Successful investor demo with zero manual workarounds
- [ ] 7 days of production stability with zero conversion failures

## Timeline

* **CAM-129**: 6.5 weeks (5 phases, can start immediately)
* **CAM-130**: TBD (faster fix, can develop in parallel)
* **Target**: Ready for next investor demo

## Dependencies

* Both issues can be developed in parallel
* Integration testing required after both complete
* E2E test suite validates complete conversion pipeline

## Related Documentation

* Incident Report: Oct 30, 2025 middleware redirect loop
* Technical Spec: specs/CAM-129-spec.md
* PRD: specs/CAM-129-prd.md

title: Setup Wizard - Navigation & Skip Functionality Bugs
description:
## Problem

Multiple critical navigation and UX issues in the Setup Wizard prevent users from completing onboarding successfully.

## Affected Components

### 1\. Navigation Buttons (CRITICAL)

* **Issue**: Cannot navigate back to update setup at certain stages
* **Impact**: Users get stuck at the Launch phase with no way to go back
* **Expected**: Previous/Back buttons should allow navigation to any prior step

### 2\. Skip Functionality (CRITICAL)

* **Issue**: Stripe setup can be skipped, but no way to go back and complete it
* **Impact**: Users who skip Stripe cannot complete payment setup within wizard OR after completing wizard
* **Expected**:
  * Option to return to skipped steps within wizard, OR
  * Clear path to complete skipped setup from dashboard after wizard completes

### 3\. Guest Booking Link Placement (UX Issue)

* **Issue**: Setup summary screen shows guest-facing booking page link (hard to see)
* **Impact**: Poor UX, users miss important link
* **Expected**: Remove link from setup summary, place prominently in Dashboard post-setup

## User Impact

**Severity**: HIGH/CRITICAL

* Blocks wizard completion if user skips required steps
* Users become stuck with no recovery path
* Occurred during live investor demo, causing manual browser refresh workarounds

## Technical Context

* **Files**:
  * `components/dashboard/setup-wizard/wizard-container.tsx`
  * `components/dashboard/setup-wizard/*-step.tsx` components
* **Related Issue**: CAM-129 (Middleware Hardening) - separate concern, can develop in parallel
* **Framework**: React 19 + Shadcn/UI + React Hook Form

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All wizard steps allow navigation back to previous steps
- [ ] Users can return to skipped steps (e.g., Stripe setup) within wizard
- [ ] Alternative: Dashboard provides clear path to complete skipped setup items
- [ ] Users cannot become permanently stuck at any wizard stage
- [ ] Guest booking link removed from setup summary
- [ ] Guest booking link added to Dashboard with prominent placement
- [ ] Navigation works on mobile devices (touch-friendly back buttons)
- [ ] Keyboard navigation works for accessibility

## Testing Requirements

- [ ] Component unit tests for navigation button handlers
- [ ] Integration tests for skip → return flow
- [ ] E2E test: Skip Stripe → Navigate back → Complete Stripe
- [ ] E2E test: Complete wizard → Verify booking link in Dashboard
- [ ] Accessibility tests (keyboard navigation, screen reader)
- [ ] Mobile responsive tests

## Dependencies

* **Blocked by**: None (can start immediately)
* **Blocks**: None (CAM-129 can proceed independently)
* **Related**: CAM-129 (middleware routing) - test together after both complete

## Priority Justification

This issue surfaced during a live investor demo where the Product Owner had to manually refresh the browser at every step to bypass navigation failures. Users who skip Stripe setup become permanently stuck with no recovery path, blocking revenue-critical payment functionality.

title: Demo Branch Strategy
description:
## Summary

Establish branching strategy for demo preparation and investor presentation to ensure stable demo environment.

## Requirements

- [ ] Create `demo` branch from stable `develop`
- [ ] Document demo branch workflow
- [ ] Establish demo data seeding process
- [ ] Create demo reset script
- [ ] Configure demo environment variables

## Demo Branch Workflow

1. Branch `demo` from `develop` 2 days before presentation
2. Cherry-pick only demo-ready features
3. Freeze commits 1 day before demo
4. Reset demo data before presentation
5. Merge improvements back to `develop` after demo

## Demo Scripts

* `scripts/demo-setup.sh` - Seed demo data
* `scripts/demo-reset.sh` - Reset to clean state
* `scripts/demo-verify.sh` - Verify all features working

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Demo branch created
- [ ] Demo scripts implemented
- [ ] Demo data seeded and tested
- [ ] Workflow documented
- [ ] Team trained on demo process

title: Branch Protection Rules
description:
## Summary

Configure branch protection rules for `main` and `develop` branches to enforce code quality and review process.

## Requirements

### Main Branch Protection

- [ ] Require pull request before merging
- [ ] Require 1 approval (if team size allows)
- [ ] Require status checks to pass
- [ ] Require conversation resolution
- [ ] No direct commits

### Develop Branch Protection

- [ ] Require pull request before merging
- [ ] Require status checks to pass
- [ ] Allow force pushes (for rebasing)

### Status Checks

- [ ] CI must pass (quality-checks)
- [ ] Unit tests must pass
- [ ] Integration tests must pass
- [ ] Build must succeed

## Note

Branch protection requires GitHub Pro or public repository. Document alternative workflow if not available.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Protection rules configured (or documented alternative)
- [ ] Team workflow documented in README
- [ ] Status checks integrated
- [ ] Process validated with test PR
